description:
## Question

Define the shape of the deliverable: its sections, what evidence each claim needs (workload, baseline status, numbers, machine), how 'defk helps' vs 'Elixir is the right choice' is decided per workload, and how the runtime contract and devex are judged. This fixes the done criterion every other ticket works towards.

comments.text:
Resolution: docs/verdict.md serves both a library go/no-go and a guide for Elixir developers. Sections: (1) Conclusion, 3-5 sentences incl. the go/no-go; (2) "Should I use defk for X?" guide by job type (Elixir / defk / Nx / Rustler), plus a traps list (poor_list_data, poor_tiny_calls, out_of_scope_word_count); (3) Workload results, a frozen snapshot tied to a commit, one row per target workload incl. poor/out_of_scope; (4) Runtime contract, one row per promise (preemption, cleanup on process death, hot code upgrade, errors as exceptions) with linked test/bench, measured figure, known gaps; (5) Developer experience, the three-part bar with evidence (error catalogue, docs/language.md with divergence page, the one rule shown consistent with every divergence) plus a cold-test log (fresh agent session with only the docs writes a new kernel); (6) Limitations and what would change the verdict; (7) Method, short, linking examples/README.md.

Workload verdict = defk vs optimised Elixir baseline, 2x bar (unchanged). Beside it, never changing it: defk vs the existing NIF (or plain C where cheap), responsiveness (worst tick gap), and Nx where it is the realistic alternative (at least one row has it).

Evidence bar per row: baseline :optimized (no provisional verdict counts), quiet-machine run_all.exs, best of N with spread, machine/OTP/Elixir/commit, Elixir attempts linked from the example header. One machine; other architectures go under Limitations.

Pre-registered go/no-go (recorded in Method before rows are filled): grow into a library only if (a) >= half the target workloads are good on optimised baselines, spanning >= 2 NIF-survey categories; (b) no open safety gap in the runtime contract (performance gaps OK); (c) devex bar met and the cold test completed a kernel from the docs alone; (d) the C-compiler-at-build-time stance is settled. Otherwise: a research result, not a library. The conclusion may argue against the rule's outcome only explicitly.

Done = every section meets its bar, run_all.exs green at the snapshot commit, and the user accepts the conclusion in a final session; then the map closes. A library effort would be a new map.

Glossary: per-workload outcome renamed "Workload verdict"; "Verdict" is docs/verdict.md (CONTEXT.md).

title: What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?
